status_summary: On 2025-01-24 the Acting Solicitor General moved the Supreme Court to hold briefing in abeyance in four pending cases so agencies could reconsider Biden-era actions; on 2025-02-06 the Court granted the motion in the Education Department borrower-defense case (No. 24-413) and denied it in the other three (Nos. 23-1229, 24-7 and 23-1067). On 2025-02-07 a Deputy Solicitor General told the Court in United States v. Skrmetti that the government's earlier equal-protection position no longer represented the United States' view while asking the Court to decide the case; the Court upheld the Tennessee law 6-3 on 2025-06-18. The Education case was dismissed on 2025-08-11 after a stipulation. These filings show the Justice Department reconsidering prior positions at the outset of the Administration; no source found shows the White House Counsel's role in those decisions.

timeline.event: The Acting Solicitor General files motions to hold the briefing schedule in abeyance in four pending cases (Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas, No. 24-413; EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining, No. 23-1229; Diamond Alternative Energy v. EPA, No. 24-7; Oklahoma v. EPA, No. 23-1067) so the agencies can reconsider the underlying actions after the change of Administration.

By orders of this date the Court grants the abeyance motion in Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas (No. 24-413) and denies it in EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining (No. 23-1229), Diamond Alternative Energy v. EPA (No. 24-7) and Oklahoma v. EPA (No. 23-1067).

A Deputy Solicitor General letter to the Court in United States v. Skrmetti (No. 23-477) says the government's earlier equal-protection arguments against Tennessee's law no longer represent the United States' position and that the new Administration would not have challenged the law; the government asks the Court to decide the question rather than dismiss.
The Court affirms the Sixth Circuit in United States v. Skrmetti (No. 23-477) by a 6-3 vote in an opinion by the Chief Justice, upholding Tennessee's law.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas (No. 24-413) is dismissed under Supreme Court Rule 46 after a stipulation of dismissal filed 2025-08-08; merits briefing had been resumed by order of 2025-06-23.

title: Have the Counsel review pending litigation and recommend reversing prior positions
uncertainties: The Skrmetti letter (signed by Deputy Solicitor General Curtis E. Gannon, the Acting Solicitor General being recused) and the supremecourt.gov docket pages for Nos. 24-413, 23-1229, 24-7 and 23-1067 were read in review. Of the 2025-01-24 motions, only the motion in No. 24-413 was read (on supremecourt.gov, 2026-10-26): it prints only January 2025 as its date (the day comes from the docket entry), credits the Acting Secretary of Education's reassessment of the borrower-defense regulations and names no White House Counsel involvement; the motions in Nos. 23-1229, 24-7 and 23-1067 were not opened. The Skrmetti decision date (2025-06-18) and 6-3 vote were confirmed in the slip opinion on supremecourt.gov (the opening portion read, which includes the syllabus and the statement of which Justices joined, concurred and dissented). The record covers a few Supreme Court cases from the first weeks; lower-court position changes were not surveyed. A 2026-08-10 news report (Reuters via NY Daily Record) of a change of White House Counsel effective 2026-09-01 is context only and says nothing of the office's litigation role. Nothing found shows what the White House Counsel recommended or when; two searches for a White House Counsel memorandum or review returned only commentary and law-firm alerts, so the match is partial and progress is held at the low end of implemented (inference): the outcome the chapter describes is visible, the Counsel's process is not. Court outcomes after the pause are context, not outcomes of the recommendation.
